figures.finding: A single resident pays national income tax from 0% on the first CHF 15,855 up to 8% above CHF 211,400; each municipality adds a surcharge of 150% to 180% of the national tax, set yearly, for a combined top rate of about 22.4%. Income includes a notional 4% of net wealth.
figures.applies: 2026; married couples and single parents have wider bands.

Communal tax is a surcharge on the national income tax due. Communities levy a surcharge of between 150% and 180%. The surcharges are fixed annually by the local governments. Consequently, the tax rate consists of the national tax rate combined with the surcharges, which results in tax rates from 2.5% to 22.4%.
Personal exemption 15,855 23,783 31,710

figures.finding: The tax year is the calendar year; the return is due in mid-April of the next year (extendable to mid-September against a provisional payment), and tax is due on assessment.

sources.said: Tax year: The tax year is the calendar year.
Filing and payment: The normal filing deadline is in mid-April of the year following the tax year.

figures.finding: The employee pays 4.70% to old-age, survivors' and disability insurance (AHV/IV) and 0.5% unemployment insurance on the first CHF 126,000; the employer pays slightly more than half of the total; occupational pension is also mandatory.

sources.said: The taxpayer’s share of social security contributions (old-age and dependent pension schemes, disability insurance) is 4.70% (with an upper limit of 18% for self-employed and employed individuals) and 0.5% for unemployment insurance on the first CHF 126,000 of compensation
The employer generally is required to pay slightly

figures.finding: Employers withhold wage tax from pay, credited against the assessed tax.

sources.said: Employers need to deduct a withholding tax (WHT) from the salary of their employees.

figures.finding: A non-resident is taxed on Liechtenstein employment income and business profits, at the national scale with a 150% municipal multiplier when assessed; there are no withholding taxes on royalties or service fees.

sources.said: Nonresidents are taxed on Liechtenstein employment income, business profits, and profits attributable to immovable property located in Liechtenstein.
For individuals with a limited tax liability who are ordinary tax-assessed, a general municipal multiplier of 150% will be applied.
There are no withholding taxes on dividends, interest, royalties, or fees for technical services in Liechtenstein, and

figures.finding: Liechtenstein applies Switzerland's VAT law with its own administration: 8.1% standard; an enterprise registers once annual turnover exceeds CHF 100,000.

sources.said: Liechtenstein has adopted the VAT law of Switzerland, while having its own VAT administration. The general VAT rate is 8.1% (7.7% up to 31 December 2023).
Registration: Enterprises whose annual turnover exceeds CHF 100,000 must, in principle, register for VAT purposes.

figures.finding: Liechtenstein has no source tax on a non-resident artiste's fee as such: a person without residence there is taxed only on the domestic income the Tax Act lists, which takes in pay for employed work done in Liechtenstein (taxed by a source deduction the Tax Administration sets, final below CHF 211,400 gross) but not a self-employed performer's or author's fee without a permanent establishment there.

employedWork.withholding: set by the Tax Administration (annual income, flat deductions, family)

figures.applies: Persons with neither residence nor habitual abode in Liechtenstein, from the Tax Act as in force on 1 July 2026 (Art. 6 para. 2 and 5, Art. 23, Art. 24, Art. 25).

figures.finding: The Tax Act gives an individual author's fees and royalties no special treatment: for a resident they are part of the income from self-employed activity taxed on the ordinary scale, and royalties paid to a non-resident are not domestic income, so nothing is withheld.
figures.applies: Resident and non-resident authors (Tax Act as in force on 1 July 2026); royalties appear in the Act only as business expenses and as passive income of companies.
